Circular-import check (the plan's hedge "assume the `gitutil` home unless the import graph makes
it circular") — **PASSED, so `gitutil` is the home**; no new `_store` leaf was created.

Evidence:

* `_store/gitutil.py` is a declared stdlib-only leaf: before the move its module level imported
  `fcntl/logging/os/random/re/subprocess/time` and no `rebar.*` module; the only rebar coupling
  was two *deferred, function-local* `from rebar._commands.fsck import _resolve_tracker_git_dir`
  calls (in `_store_git_lock_path` and `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`). Both are now gone.
* Each moved primitive preserves that property. `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` and `_ticket_dirs`
  need only `os`. `_dir_is_archived` needs `rebar.reducer._api._is_net_archived`, and that import
  was **already function-local** in `fsck_repair`; it stays function-local in `gitutil`, so the
  module still has zero module-level `rebar.*` imports.
* Every consumer is a `_commands` module importing `_store` — the direction that already existed
  (`fsck_repair` has imported `run_git` from `gitutil` at module level all along).
* Mechanically verified by AC6: `python -c "import rebar._store.gitutil"` exits 0 and
  `! grep -qE '^(from|import) rebar' src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` exits 0.

Scope corrections the plan review forced (all folded into the revised description + file_impact,
which now lists 8 files, not 5):

* The original "four consumers" undercounted. Three more production modules imported the
  primitives **directly from `fsck_repair`** via deferred function-local imports and were
  invisible to the plan: `compact.py` (`_ticket_dirs`), `bridge_repair.py` and
  `tracker_maintenance.py` (`_resolve_tracker_git_dir`). All three are repointed at `gitutil`
  rather than left riding a compat re-export — leaving them would preserve the exact inverted
  dependency this ticket removes.
* `_dir_is_archived` is a **third** primitive that had to move: `_ticket_dirs` calls it and
  `fsck_scan` imports it directly. Moving only the two named symbols would have left `gitutil`
  importing `_dir_is_archived` back out of `fsck_repair`.

Compatibility surfaces preserved — **two**, not one. `fsck.py`'s re-export was documented; the
second was not, and only a raw grep found it (Serena returns the LSP reference set and silently
omits string-named bindings, exactly the asymmetry AGENTS.md warns about). Three tests bind the
names as **`fsck_repair` module attributes**:
`monkeypatch.setattr(fsck_repair, "_ticket_dirs"/"_resolve_tracker_git_dir", ...)` in
`tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` and
`tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py`, plus
`_fsck_repair._ticket_dirs(...)` in `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py`. `fsck_repair` therefore
keeps module-level re-imports of all three names from `gitutil` (with `# noqa: F401`, the same
pattern `fsck.py` already uses), so those patches still take effect on `fsck_repair`'s own call
sites and no test file needed editing (AC7).

RED -> GREEN oracle (the move has no new behaviour, so the AC set is the oracle). On the
unmodified worktree at `origin/main` 09abac96: AC1 FAIL, AC2 FAIL, AC3 FAIL, AC4-AC7/AC12 PASS
(the compat invariants, which must never go red). After the move: all of AC1-AC7 and AC12 PASS.
AC3 is checked with an `ast`-based import walk rather than the line-anchored grep in the
description, because the plan review correctly noted a line-anchored pattern misses the
parenthesized multi-line imports `fsck_scan.py` and `fsck.py` actually use.

Function bodies moved verbatim — confirmed by unparsing both revisions' ASTs with docstrings
stripped: `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`, `_ticket_dirs` and `_dir_is_archived` are all code-identical
to `origin/main`. The only text change is an added paragraph on `_dir_is_archived`'s docstring
recording why its reducer import must stay function-local.

Module sizes after the move: `gitutil.py` 614 -> 672 LOC, `fsck_repair.py` 686 -> 653 LOC; both
well under the 800-LOC cap (AC12). Complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

Gate results for the implementation (Gerrit change 1920, patch set 1, commit 9fbacaa2da).

AC8 `make lint`: PASS. AC9 `make typecheck`: PASS (mypy, 568 source files, no issues).
AC10 complexity ratchet: PASS — `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`. AC12 module sizes:
`gitutil.py` 671 LOC, `fsck_repair.py` 652 LOC, both under the 800 cap.

AC11 `pytest -m 'not integration and not external'`: **14314 passed, 55 skipped, 1 xfailed,
0 failures, 0 errors** in 607s.

A note on how that number was reached, because the first two runs were noisy and the noise was
mine, not the code's. Live Jira credentials (`JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN`) were
present in the shell, so every run explicitly deselected `live`, `jira_live`, `external`,
`llm_live` and `integration` and additionally ran with those three variables unset, rather than
relying on the live tests' own self-skip. An earlier parallel run reported 19 errors; all 19 were
harness artifacts I caused — 18 were `Test moved the repo HEAD (09abac969c -> 9fbacaa2da)`,
tripped because I ran `git commit` while the suite was still running, and the 19th was a
`.pytest_cache` leak into REPO_ROOT from a second pytest process I had started concurrently.
Re-run once with a stable HEAD, no concurrent session and `-p no:cacheprovider`, the suite is
completely clean. No test file was touched (AC7).

Targeted confirmation of the compatibility surfaces, run separately: the 60 tests across
`test_scan_scoping.py`, `test_repair_pause_ownership.py`,
`test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py`, `test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py`,
`test_event_append_transient_retry.py` and `test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py` — i.e.
every test that binds the moved symbols through `fsck.<symbol>` or as an `fsck_repair` module
attribute — all pass.

Gerrit `LLM-Review`: **+1 (PASS)**, with one non-blocking advisory, already auto-resolved: the
`_dir_is_archived` re-export in `fsck_repair` is unused in that module's body and, unlike the
other two names, is not patched by any test. That is accurate. It is kept deliberately, to
preserve `fsck_repair`'s pre-move module-attribute surface whole (`fsck_scan` imported
`_dir_is_archived` from there before this change) and because AC5 as signed asserts all three
names still resolve on `fsck_repair`. It carries `# noqa: F401`, the same pattern `fsck.py`
already uses for its re-exports. Left as-is rather than amended, since the finding is advisory
and resolved and an amend would discard an in-flight CI run.

compiled_state.description:
# Move fsck's shared filesystem primitives out of `fsck_repair.py`

## Context / Problem

Surfaced by the architectural analysis on `defaceable-icy-antelope`. Three pure filesystem
primitives live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`:

- `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` — resolve the tracker's git dir (handles the worktree pointer file);
- `_ticket_dirs` — the shared store-walk iterator (sorted ticket dirs, active-only by default);
- `_dir_is_archived` — the archival predicate `_ticket_dirs` filters with, and `fsck_scan`'s own
  import.

They are there for a historical reason, not a structural one: `fsck_repair` was the first module
extracted out of `fsck.py`. The result is an inverted dependency — none of the three has anything
to do with repair, yet **seven** production modules reach into the **repair** module for them:

| consumer | symbols | how |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py` | `_dir_is_archived`, `_ticket_dirs`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` | `_ticket_dirs`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level re-export, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | **two** function-local imports, from `fsck` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level, from `fsck` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` | `_ticket_dirs` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/bridge_repair.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |

So a store-layer module (`gitutil`) depends on a command-layer *repair* module to answer 'where
is the tracker's git dir', and the diagnostic path cannot be read without loading the mutating
one. A future non-fsck caller would have no reason to look for these under 'repair'.

## Approach

Move all three primitives to `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` and repoint every consumer.

**Why `gitutil`, and the circular-import check the move is conditioned on.** `gitutil` is a
declared stdlib-only leaf: its module level imports `fcntl`/`logging`/`os`/`random`/`re`/
`subprocess`/`time` and **no** `rebar.*` module. Each moved primitive keeps that property:
`_resolve_tracker_git_dir` and `_ticket_dirs` need only `os`, and `_dir_is_archived`'s
`rebar.reducer._api._is_net_archived` import is already **function-local** and stays that way.
Every consumer is a `_commands` module importing `_store`, which is the direction that already
exists (`fsck_repair` imports `run_git` from `gitutil` at module level today). So the graph is
acyclic and the `gitutil` default holds; a new `_store` leaf is not needed and would land under
AGENTS.md's "never create files < 100 LOC by splitting" rule. AC6 checks this mechanically.

**Module size.** `gitutil` 614 -> ~665 LOC, `fsck_repair` 686 -> ~640 LOC; both stay under the
800-LOC hard cap.

**Compatibility surfaces that must survive — two, not one.**

1. `fsck.py` keeps re-exporting `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (now imported from
   `gitutil`), so `fsck.<symbol>` attribute access keeps resolving. That surface is documented in
   the architectural-analysis comment on `defaceable-icy-antelope`, and is bound by
   `test_event_append_transient_retry.py`, `test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py`,
   `test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py` and `test_concurrency_regression.py`.
2. `fsck_repair.py` keeps **module-level bindings** for all three names (re-imported from
   `gitutil`). This is load-bearing and easy to miss: three tests bind the names as *module
   attributes on `fsck_repair`*, which the LSP cannot see — `monkeypatch.setattr(fsck_repair,
   "_ticket_dirs", ...)` / `..., "_resolve_tracker_git_dir", ...)` in
   `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` and
   `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py`, and
   `_fsck_repair._ticket_dirs(...)` in `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py`. Keeping them as
   `fsck_repair` module globals means those patches still take effect on `fsck_repair`'s own
   call sites (which resolve through the module global), so no test file needs editing (AC7).

The three function-local importers (`compact`, `bridge_repair`, `tracker_maintenance`) are
repointed at `gitutil` rather than left riding `fsck_repair`'s compat re-import — leaving them
would preserve the very inverted dependency this ticket removes.

Behaviour-preserving: no logic change, function bodies moved verbatim, imports repointed only.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the existing suite is the oracle and is run **unmodified** (AC7). The
executable RED oracle for the move itself is the AC grep set: AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 all fail on
`origin/main` and pass after the move, and that before/after run is recorded as a ticket comment.

The bindings at risk are the eight test files named above plus the fsck suites under
`tests/interfaces/store/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: none of the three primitives is defined in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` —
      verified by
      `! grep -qE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC2: all three are defined in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — verified by
      `test "$(grep -cE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py)" = 3`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC3: no module under `src/rebar/` imports any of the three from `fsck` or `fsck_repair` —
      verified by
      `! grep -rqE 'from rebar\._commands\.fsck(_repair)? import.*(_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/`
      exiting 0. (This covers the seven consumers, including the three function-local importers
      `compact.py`, `bridge_repair.py` and `tracker_maintenance.py`.)
- [ ] AC4: the `fsck` re-export surface still resolves — verified by
      `python -c "from rebar._commands import fsck; fsck._resolve_tracker_git_dir; fsck._ticket_dirs"`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC5: the `fsck_repair` module-attribute surface the un-editable tests patch still resolves —
      verified by
      `python -c "from rebar._commands import fsck_repair; fsck_repair._resolve_tracker_git_dir; fsck_repair._ticket_dirs; fsck_repair._dir_is_archived"`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC6: the new home introduced no cycle and `gitutil` is still a stdlib-only leaf — verified by
      `python -c "import rebar._store.gitutil"` exiting 0 AND
      `! grep -qE '^(from|import) rebar' src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] AC7: no test file is edited — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` producing
      no output.
- [ ] AC8: `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] AC9: `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] AC10: `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 (no `new`/`increased`).
- [ ] AC11: `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exits 0.
- [ ] AC12: every `src/rebar` file stays under the 800-LOC cap — verified by the CI module-size
      gate; locally `wc -l src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` both
      report < 800.

Repoint the _resolve_tracker_git_dir import at the new home
